agent-mailbox.summary: Coordinates agents through append-only messages in a shared folder.
when: Agents need an auditable exchange across runtimes.
An existing room needs reconciliation.
avoid: A one-shot handoff suffices; this is not a transport or authentication service.
agent-mailbox.example: /agent-mailbox Coordinate with the other agent in our shared room.
steps: Identify room, participants, objective, transport and ownership.
Use the canonical handshake for a new room or genuinely new participant; returning participants resume and reconcile without repeating it.
Reconcile addressed messages and record durable dispositions.
Use bounded listening only when proven, and report parked or degraded continuity.

delegation.detail: Two or more agents exchange messages. Bounded listening is optional, participant-local and requires proven support; ordinary Standard Exchange works without it.

agent-mailbox.outputs: Messages, dispositions, primer and continuity status.

agent-output.summary: Compresses agent-to-agent reports while preserving decision-critical evidence and caveats.
when: A worker must report an outcome or blocker.
A reviewer must communicate actionable findings.
avoid: You need human-facing prose or message transport.
steps: Lead with state and result.
Include exact evidence, changes and material gaps.
Give the next action while retaining scope, uncertainty and gates.

delegation.detail: The contract does not dispatch agents.

ask-gate.summary: Triages a pending question and prepares it according to stakes.
when: You are about to ask the Handler.
A consequential decision needs sound framing.
avoid: The answer can be resolved from the request or available context.
ask-gate.example: /ask-gate Check whether I should ask about this choice.
steps: Resolve answerable questions without asking.
Classify necessary questions as routine or high stakes.
Use the checklist for routine questions, or critique and assess high-stakes options.
Ask a clear, appropriately framed question.

delegation.detail: Deliberation does not require a subagent.

ask-gate.outputs: A resolved choice or quality-checked question.

when: A timeout or threshold changes
Comments require values to stay synchronized
avoid: A single imported constant is compiler-enforced
audit-coupled-constant.example: /audit-coupled-constant check the retry timeout across this repository
steps: List all representations and units
Search each representation across the relevant scope
Classify hits and repair missed sites and bidirectional references
Report evidence and intentional differences

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

audit-coupled-constant.outputs: A classified audit report and any authorized repairs.

budget-check.summary: Checks usage before an expensive agent wave, returning go, no-go or unknown.
when: A large fan-out is planned.
You have a token ceiling to test.
avoid: You need an authoritative billing or plan-quota reading.
budget-check.example: /budget-check Check whether this agent wave can start.
steps: Run the bundled usage wrapper with a threshold and actual token limit when known.
Read the active block, ceiling and verdict.
Reduce or defer a no-go wave; never treat unknown as go.

delegation.detail: The check does not dispatch agents.

caller-options.summary: Routes one skill invocation among viable modes and execution venues.
when: A skill declares meaningful venue choices.
A skill has multiple viable execution paths.
avoid: You are selecting a persistent session mode.
caller-options.example: /caller-options Route this investigation between inline and delegated execution.
steps: Triage choices and proceed directly if one dominates.
Eliminate unavailable or unsafe combinations and compare survivors.
Surface material choices and execute the selected path.
For delegation, use the resolved marker and inspect the result.

delegation.detail: Delegated or fan-out venues may be selected; self-orchestrators are not wrapped.

cold-review.summary: Reviews actual work against objectives using fresh independent perspectives.
when: Completed work needs outside review.
You need evidence-backed findings before acceptance.
avoid: You need a quick check of one claim.
cold-review.example: /cold-review Review this implementation against its objective.
steps: Classify the work and choose review breadth.
Brief fresh reviewers on objectives and artifacts when available; otherwise label the same-session review degraded.
Reopen evidence when synthesizing and verify findings.
Report coverage, findings, score and threshold verdict.

delegation.detail: Use fresh reviewers when supported and appropriate; if unavailable, perform and label a degraded same-session review. More than three reviewers requires confirmation.

defuddle.summary: Extract readable Markdown from a web page.
when: Read an article or blog post
Extract a documentation page
avoid: API responses or raw downloads
steps: Supply the URL
Run the Markdown extraction and inspect the result
Use an available alternative or report a gap if the CLI is missing

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

defuddle.outputs: Clean page content or requested metadata.

design-an-interface.summary: Compare concrete module interfaces and synthesize a recommendation.
when: Design a nontrivial API
Compare module boundaries
avoid: Implementing the chosen internals
design-an-interface.example: /design-an-interface compare interfaces for a file upload module
steps: Establish callers, cases, failures and constraints
Produce three different designs with signatures and examples
Compare tradeoffs and synthesize a concrete recommendation
Ask whether the result fits the primary use case

delegation.detail: Use independent subagents when available; otherwise develop each design sequentially without cross-contamination.

diff-recap.summary: Summarize an actual Git diff as a reconciled, pasteable recap.
when: Prepare a pull request summary
Explain file-level changes
avoid: A substitute for reviewing correctness
diff-recap.example: /diff-recap summarize the changes on this branch
steps: Capture file status and counts directly from Git for the selected diff
Group and label rows without inventing intent
Validate rows and totals with the bundled value gate; fail closed if the diff is empty or unavailable
Render the appropriate human or agent output

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

diff-recap.outputs: An evidence-backed recap with file rows and totals.

directives-audit.summary: Audits directive systems for authority, scope, safety, routing and drift.
when: You need a read-only directive assessment.
You explicitly request housekeeping of selected findings.
avoid: The concern is skill behavior or prose alone.
steps: Inventory sources, routes, owners and consumed forms.
Traverse each in-scope edge and name gaps.
Report findings with evidence and ownership.
Housekeep only on explicit request and follow its mutation gate.

delegation.detail: Delegation is not a condition of the audit.

directives-audit.outputs: An audit and, if explicitly requested, approved housekeeping.

domain-check.summary: Reconcile domain availability signals using registration and DNS evidence.
when: Check a candidate domain
Investigate disagreement between lookup providers
avoid: Treating DNS silence as proof of availability
steps: Query registration data and relevant DNS resolvers
Apply the documented evidence precedence and fallbacks
Report uncertainty, coverage gaps and conflicting signals

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

domain-check.outputs: A qualified availability assessment with sources.

double-check.summary: Re-examines a claim, output or decision against fresh evidence.
when: A claim needs a targeted re-check.
You want assumptions challenged before relying on an output.
avoid: You need a formal phase gate.
steps: Identify a clear target and reread it.
Challenge assumptions and cross-check sources.
Iterate on issues and report a verdict with evidence and uncertainty.

delegation.detail: Caller Options can select inline or delegated checking.

extract-signal.summary: Turns noisy sources into vetted signal in the requested form.
when: You need evidence gathered for a decision.
Audience, stakes and destination can be identified.
avoid: You need only a raw fetch.
extract-signal.example: /extract-signal Extract the signal from these complaints as a decision brief.
steps: Infer the signal, audience, stakes and destination.
Compose appropriate gathering and vetting methods.
Report provenance, confidence and gaps, matching sensitivity to destination.

delegation.detail: Normal calls default to a fresh subagent; when the skill is the active agent it works inline.

extract-signal.outputs: A vetted signal in the requested form.

freshness-contract.summary: Determines whether old evidence remains usable for a current decision.
when: You are about to reuse a prior test or report.
Intervening changes may invalidate evidence.
avoid: You need to establish a new claim from scratch.
freshness-contract.example: /freshness-contract Check whether yesterday's test still supports release.
steps: Classify the artifact and decision.
Identify age anchors, intervening changes and invalidators.
Apply the restrictive table: reuse, spot-check or re-verify; accept labeled risk only in the no-cheap-discriminator case.

delegation.detail: This lookup does not prescribe delegation.

freshness-contract.outputs: A freshness decision and required follow-up.

github-sync.summary: Reviews session changes, obtains approval for commits, then commits and pushes.
when: You want selected changes committed and pushed.
The destination and outgoing commits need review.
avoid: You want commit-only work or partial staging.
github-sync.example: /github-sync Commit and push this session's approved changes.
steps: Inspect changes, destination and all outgoing commits.
Group intended changes and exclude unrelated or unsafe files.
Present the destination, complete outgoing set and exact full ordered commit messages; obtain explicit approval for that plan.
Stage approved paths, check messages and attribution, push and report.

delegation.detail: The workflow does not require subagents.

github-sync.outputs: Approved commits pushed or a reported stop.

handoff.summary: Creates a structured brief for a fresh agent or session.
when: An autonomous task needs transferring.
You are switching sessions or packaging parallel work.
avoid: The current session should simply become coordinator.
handoff.example: /handoff Create a handoff for the remaining import flow.
steps: Identify objective, profile, scope and constraints.
Gather required sources and acceptance checks; an empty required-source list needs explicit confirmation and yields advisory mode.
Write and verify the structured brief.
Provide the artifact and activation phrase.

delegation.detail: An orchestrator profile can describe parallel tasks; writing a brief does not dispatch them.

handoff.outputs: A handoff file and chat surface.

handoff-execute.summary: Executes a structured handoff with source ingestion and acceptance verification.
when: A fresh session receives a handoff.
The brief specifies required sources and an outcome.
avoid: The input is a normal plan or an independent review request.
handoff-execute.example: /handoff-execute Execute the handoff at the supplied path.
steps: Read the brief and required sources before planning; unresolved or unreadable required sources block by default, while explicit force permits labeled degraded execution.
Cite sources in the execution plan.
Execute within bounds and run outcome verification.
Report the ground-truth retrospective and gaps.

delegation.detail: Follow the handoff profile; delegation is not universal.

handoff-execute.outputs: Completed work, outcome verification and a ground-truth retro; a failed retro write falls back to chat with a write-failure record.

headless-claude.summary: Run a bounded Claude Code CLI task under a supervisor.
when: Delegate a scoped inspection
Run an authorized file task
avoid: Unsupervised processes or silent billing changes
headless-claude.example: /headless-claude inspect the parser for edge cases
steps: Check CLI access, help, model and required permissions
Define exact scope, deadline, tools and cancellation
Launch under a retained supervisor and monitor output
Validate the result and report limitations

delegation.detail: The delegated worker is a supervised provider CLI process, not a native subagent. Nested delegation requires separate authorization and bounds.

headless-claude.outputs: Captured process evidence and the requested verified result.

headless-codex.summary: Run a bounded Codex CLI task with scoped authority.
when: Delegate a focused code task
Run a bounded analysis
avoid: Assuming process success proves artifact correctness
headless-codex.example: /headless-codex review the test failures in this package
steps: Inspect CLI access, configuration, model and permissions
Set explicit scope, deadline and supervision
Capture events and monitor the child through completion
Verify the requested result independently

delegation.detail: The delegated worker is a supervised provider CLI process, not a native subagent. Nested delegation requires separate authorization and bounds.

headless-codex.outputs: Run evidence, result and access or execution gaps.

headless-gemini.summary: Run a bounded Gemini or Claude task through Antigravity CLI (agy), using a locally available model and a capable supervisor.
when: Delegate a scoped analysis
Run an authorized workspace task
avoid: You need the separate gemini CLI rather than Antigravity CLI (agy).
You require enforced read-only or exact tool isolation without an independently verified boundary.
Treating an added directory as an access allowlist.
headless-gemini.example: /headless-gemini summarize the architecture of this project
steps: Check the installed Antigravity CLI, authentication, model access and effective configuration.
Set exact authorized tools and paths; stop when required isolation cannot be independently established.
Otherwise disclose that monitoring detects actions after dispatch, then launch a bounded supervised task.
Validate the output and report limitations and gaps.

delegation.detail: The delegated worker is a supervised provider CLI process, not a native subagent. Nested delegation requires separate authorization and bounds; disclose when native usage ceilings are unavailable.

headless-gemini.outputs: A bounded child result with supervision and permission evidence.

headless-grok.summary: Run a bounded Grok Build CLI task using selected permissions.
when: Delegate a focused CLI task
Run a restricted analysis
avoid: Assuming subscription access grants API entitlement
headless-grok.example: /headless-grok inspect this module for error handling
steps: Check installed CLI, authentication and model access.
Choose a minimal approved tool and path scope; Windows containment is unestablished, so stop if enforced read-only or exact isolation is required without independent proof.
Otherwise disclose that monitoring detects actions after dispatch, then launch and supervise the retained process.
Inspect tool use and validate the result.

delegation.detail: The delegated worker is a supervised provider CLI process, not a native subagent. Nested delegation requires separate authorization and bounds.

headless-grok.outputs: Captured output and a report of identity, limits and gaps.

headless-models.summary: Select a headless model using capability, cost and availability evidence.
when: Compare providers for a task
Choose a model and effort
avoid: Refreshing the catalog itself
headless-models.example: /headless-models recommend a model for a bounded code review
steps: Define output needs and constraints
Check current provider evidence and local availability separately
Compare suitable choices and disclose cost uncertainty
Recommend a supported route without changing the caller's selection

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

headless-models.outputs: A sourced model and effort recommendation.

headless-update-models.summary: Refresh canonical headless model evidence and consumer projections.
when: Update family model guidance
Refresh stale provider evidence
avoid: Live quota checks or benchmark inference
steps: Identify the canonical source and exact write cohort, including established copied or plugin installations.
Gather current primary model, pricing and benchmark evidence without benchmark inference.
Update dated records, project them to registered headless consumers, and refresh the selected established installations through verified installers while retaining preimages.
The explicit update request authorizes that scope; new installations require a separate request.
Verify source and installed parity and report gaps.

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

headless-update-models.outputs: Updated guidance and a dated coverage and parity report.

headless-usage.summary: Read available account usage and reset information across supported harnesses.
when: Check remaining quotas
Compare returned usage windows
avoid: Estimating request counts or enabling paid overage
steps: Discover available authenticated usage surfaces without inference or credential-store access.

Prefer the Codex desktop usage tool when available; otherwise use the Windows direct reader for Codex. Use that reader for Antigravity on Windows, or verified native surfaces on other platforms; report unavailable routes.
For Claude or Grok, inspect an existing usage surface or use a bounded supervised terminal session; Grok startup hooks and MCP integrations may run.
Distinguish live, cached, unverified and unavailable readings; report timestamps, reset windows and gaps.

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

headless-usage.outputs: A dated quota table with source and freshness labels.

human-draw.summary: Turns relational, positional, or proportional information into a text figure that carries meaning alongside concise prose.
when: Relationships, sequence, branching, or proportion are central.
You need a compact figure legible in a monospace transcript.
avoid: The material is records with shared attributes; use a table.
You need a rendered chart for a graphical surface.
human-draw.example: /human-draw Show the three rollout stages and rollback branches as a diagram.
steps: Choose the shape matching the information.
Read the selected shape guidance and encode it in printable ASCII.
Keep labels and values informative if the figure wraps.
Check width, glyphs, alignment, arithmetic, node limits, and honesty.
Return the figure with its check receipt and surrounding explanation.

delegation.detail: Defines a figure-design workflow and no subagent step.

human-draw.outputs: A checked ASCII figure with explanation; it supplements prose and adds no unsupported facts.

human-merge.summary: Combines reports into one decision-ready account while accounting for shared sources, superseded claims, conflicts, and pooled gaps.
when: You have multiple reports, research summaries, or agent results on one subject.
You need to know which findings are independent, contradicted, outdated, or collectively missing.
avoid: You have one text to simplify without changing claims; use human-rewrite.
You need only the writing contract for a new report; use human-output.
human-merge.example: /human-merge Combine these three review reports and show which evidence is independent.
steps: Inventory each input, its basis, author/date, and known shared sources.
Reconcile definitions and distinguish repeated claims from independent evidence.
Classify conflicts and order superseded findings without averaging disagreement away.
Pool coverage to reveal gaps absent from individual reports.
Present combined findings and limits in decision-relevant order.

delegation.detail: Merges reports that may come from agents but does not prescribe spawning or delegating work.

human-merge.outputs: A consolidated report with source dependence, supersessions, conflict types, pooled coverage, and uncertainty.

human-output.summary: Guides writing as it happens so a reader can understand the decision, consequence, evidence, and unchecked scope.
when: You are preparing an answer, report, finding, or decision request.
You want the verdict and decision-changing caveat visible immediately.
avoid: You need to repair existing text while preserving claims; use human-rewrite.
You need to combine reports or draw relationships; use human-merge or human-draw.
human-output.example: /human-output Write a concise decision memo on whether to accept this vendor proposal.
steps: Lead with the verdict and any caveat that could reverse it.
State the ask or next action, then explain what it means.
Order details by decision relevance and put claims before supporting evidence.
Label confirmed claims, judgments, and estimates; state what was not checked.
Keep reference detail below the decision and mechanically check figures when present.

delegation.detail: Defines reader-facing writing practices and no subagent workflow.

human-output.outputs: A reader-oriented response with decision, action, consequences, evidence, and unchecked scope.

human-rewrite.summary: Repairs existing text so a person can read and act on it while preserving its claims and degree of certainty.
when: An existing report or answer is too dense, confusing, or hard to act on.
You need a clearer version that preserves numbers, scope, attribution, and caveats.
avoid: You need to merge reports and reconcile claims; use human-merge.
You want fresh writing rather than a meaning-preserving repair; use human-output.
human-rewrite.example: /human-rewrite Rewrite this update so a client can see the decision and what remains uncertain.
steps: Identify the reader, decision need, and what makes the text hard to use.
Preserve claim strength, attribution, scope, numbers, units, uncertainty, and caveats.
Resolve shorthand and reorder by decision relevance without changing claims.
Restack for the destination while retaining necessary supporting detail.
Check fidelity and name unresolved ambiguity or missing source context.

delegation.detail: Transforms supplied or existing text and defines no subagent step.

human-rewrite.outputs: A clearer meaning-preserving rewrite with caveats and evidence limits intact.

improve-codebase-architecture.summary: Find opportunities to deepen modules and reduce coupling.
when: Investigate brittle tests
Explore a targeted architectural refactor
avoid: Implementing a candidate before selection
improve-codebase-architecture.example: /improve-codebase-architecture find coupling in the upload module
steps: Explore the code and identify candidates
Present candidates and let the user select one
Frame dependencies and design alternative interfaces
Compare designs and develop the selected direction
Draft the RFC; create a GitHub issue only after explicit confirmation, or provide the draft for manual use.

delegation.detail: Use independent subagents when available; otherwise develop each design sequentially without cross-contamination.

improve-codebase-architecture.outputs: Evidence-backed candidates, a selected design and an RFC draft; a GitHub issue only when explicitly approved.

insight-adversarial.summary: Stress-tests a plan, design, document, workflow, or system through distinct critic personas and synthesizes findings into a verdict.
when: You want a red-team or multi-angle challenge.
You want rigorous scrutiny of assumptions, failure points, or objections.
avoid: You want a focused review of one output; use insight-critique.
You want unseen frames rather than attacks; use insight-angles.
insight-adversarial.example: /insight-adversarial Stress-test this rollout plan for the strongest objections.
steps: Classify the target and choose distinct relevant personas.
Run focused critiques with specific findings.
Synthesize non-duplicate risks while retaining disagreements.
Apply the pass rules and return the verdict and next step.

delegation.detail: Caller Options resolves inline or delegated venue for the invocation; the skill specifies no automatic fan-out.

insight-adversarial.outputs: A multi-persona critique with findings, synthesis, verdict, and next step.

insight-angles.summary: Finds less-visible frames, connections, assumptions, candidate expansions, and second-order effects around a subject.
when: You want to widen or reframe a subject.
You want connections surfaced before choosing an option.
avoid: You want implementation alternatives; use insight-explore.
You want flaw-focused review or a decision over options; use insight-adversarial or insight-cross-examine.
insight-angles.example: /insight-angles Find missing perspectives and connections in this proposal.
steps: Frame the subject and current view.
Classify domain, type, maturity, and current trends.
Choose roster and subject-specific lenses; note skips.
Run context-appropriate passes and connect and score findings.
Return an angle map and synthesis.

delegation.detail: Selects inline or cold isolated-worker passes by subject; asks when uncertain. Quick/resolved runs are inline. Deep passes and fan-out above about six workers require Handler consent. Cold workers each handle one lens and do not delegate.

insight-angles.outputs: An angle map of frames, typed connections, assumptions, expansions, and second-order effects with a synthesis.

insight-assess.summary: Evaluates an approach, decision, implementation, or options against relevant criteria and recommends a course.
when: You already have an option or decision to evaluate.
You need a comparison, impact analysis, or supported recommendation.
avoid: You need to generate alternatives first; use insight-explore.
You want focused review of one output; use insight-critique.
insight-assess.example: /insight-assess Compare these two storage approaches for our service.
steps: Frame the decision, objectives, constraints, and evidence.
Compare options across consistent relevant dimensions.
Use optional methods only when requested or useful.
Check alignment and identify assumptions or gaps.
Give a supported verdict, rationale, and conditions or alternatives.

delegation.detail: Defines an evidence-based assessment flow and no subagent step.

insight-assess.outputs: A verdict, rationale, conditions or alternatives, and material evidence and uncertainty.

insight-critique.summary: Reviews one existing plan, code change, architecture, or UI output and reports strengths, risks, and fixes.
when: You want focused feedback on a specific output.
You want a quality review before proceeding.
avoid: You want multi-persona stress testing; use insight-adversarial.
You need to generate or compare options; use insight-explore or insight-assess.
insight-critique.example: /insight-critique Review this API migration plan for gaps.
steps: Classify the subject as code, plan, architecture, or UI.
Summarize purpose, scope, and approach.
Identify specific strengths and rank risks.
Pair risks with concrete must-fix or optional fixes.
Return the report and verdict.

delegation.detail: Caller Options resolves inline or delegated venue for the invocation.

insight-critique.outputs: A Summary, Strengths, Risks, and Fixes report with Approved, Conditional, or Not Approved verdict.

insight-cross-examine.summary: Routes a subject or option set through depth-scaled deliberation, discovers angles, critiques and assesses choices, then recommends.
when: You want a recommendation across candidates or a complex decision.
You want discovery and critique combined without running every method by default.
avoid: You want only one critique, assessment, or brainstorm; use that focused skill.
You want phase-by-phase inspection of an existing plan; use plan-deep-dive.
insight-cross-examine.example: /insight-cross-examine Weigh these vendor options and recommend one.
steps: Classify the question and evidence context; select depth.
Discover angles inline at the selected depth.
Run only selected critique, assessment, or one relevant specialist method.
For sets, compare consistently and consider justified hybrids.
Report recommendation, alternatives, uncertainty, and coverage.

delegation.detail: Normal sub-skills run inline. Large-set fan-out, L5 depth, and extra reassessment are offered for explicit consent and never automatic.

insight-cross-examine.outputs: A decision surface with recommendation, alternatives, decisive assumptions, coverage, and analysis trail.

insight-explore.summary: Generates distinct approaches to a problem and compares them before a plan is chosen.
when: You want a brainstorm of ways to solve a problem.
You need plausible alternatives before committing.
avoid: You have fixed options to evaluate; use insight-assess.
You need a detailed implementation plan; use plan-create.
insight-explore.example: /insight-explore Explore three ways to add offline support to this app.
steps: Clarify constraints, requirements, and preferences.
Generate distinct approaches, including standard, performance-oriented, and minimal options where useful.
Compare on developer experience, robustness, timeline, and alignment.
Recommend a winner and suggest the next step.

delegation.detail: Specifies ideation and comparison, with no subagent step.

insight-explore.outputs: Distinct options, comparison, recommendation, and proposed next step; no code or implementation plan.

insight-premortem.summary: Imagines a plan has failed and identifies plausible causes, evidence gaps, and ways to prevent or detect them.
when: You want to identify future failure paths before committing.
You need warning signs and response triggers for a proposed plan.
avoid: The failure has happened and needs causal investigation; use insight-root-cause.
You want broad post-implementation learning; use insight-retro.
insight-premortem.example: /insight-premortem Assume this migration failed six months from now. What likely happened?
steps: Name the plan, constraints, intended result, and observable failure.
Generate plausible causes before mitigations.
Check causes against assumptions, evidence, counterevidence, and missing perspectives.
Prioritize and propose prevention, warnings, responses, and residual risks.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; tasks are bounded, read-only, non-overlapping, and have no nested delegation.

insight-premortem.outputs: Failure paths, evidence status, proposed mitigations and warning signs, residual risks, and gaps; no plan edits.

insight-reference-class.summary: Forecasts an outcome from comparable completed cases and explains differences from the current plan's estimate.
when: You want an outside-view forecast based on past cases.
You want to check whether a schedule, cost, or outcome estimate is optimistic.
avoid: You want to assess whether more research is worth its cost; use insight-value-of-information.
You lack a defensible comparison set and need a numeric forecast.
insight-reference-class.example: /insight-reference-class Estimate likely delivery range from comparable completed migrations.
steps: Define outcome, units, horizon, decision, and comparability criteria.
Build a traceable set of comparable completed cases, noting failures and exclusions.
Show the supported observed range or distribution.
Compare with the inside view and explain adjustments, limits, and what could change the estimate.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; useful slices include case retrieval, selection challenge, and calculation checks.

insight-reference-class.outputs: An outside-view estimate or evidence-insufficient conclusion with sources, limits, adjustments, and sensitivity.

insight-retro.summary: Reviews significant completed implementation work to map impact, capture patterns, check documentation, and list follow-up work.
when: A substantial implementation has finished and its effects should be recorded.
You need to check documentation, reusable knowledge, difficulty, and technical debt.
avoid: You only want candidate skill gaps; use insight-skill-gap.
There is no reliable inventory of completed changes yet.
insight-retro.example: /insight-retro Review the completed authentication rollout and identify follow-up work.
steps: Map changed packages, files, interfaces, and effects.
Extract reusable patterns and recommend skill, documentation, or no action.
Audit documentation and knowledge items against the change map.
Assess execution difficulty and technical debt.
Return findings with gate status and unverified criteria.

delegation.detail: Specifies a retrospective workflow and no subagent step.

insight-retro.outputs: Blast-radius summary, pattern and documentation findings, knowledge updates, difficulty notes, technical debt, and gate status.

insight-root-cause.summary: Investigates an observed or recurring problem by tracing evidence-linked causes and competing explanations.
when: You want to explain why an observed problem occurred.
You need supported causes separated from contributors and open hypotheses.
avoid: The event is hypothetical; use insight-premortem.
You want broad lessons after an implementation; use insight-retro.
insight-root-cause.example: /insight-root-cause Find why the scheduled import keeps stopping early.
steps: Describe the event, expected behavior, timeframe, scope, and impact.
Build causal hypotheses with evidence and a disconfirming check for each link.
Challenge timing, mechanism, and competing explanations.
Report supported causes separately and propose a test or countermeasure without running it.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; possible slices include timeline, alternative causes, and disconfirmation.

insight-root-cause.outputs: Evidence-linked causal account, unresolved hypotheses, and proposed checks or countermeasures.

insight-skill-gap.summary: Compares recent work with the existing skill index to find reusable patterns that are missing or under-covered.
when: You want to know whether recent work exposed a skill gap.
A retrospective identified patterns worth comparing with existing skills.
avoid: You want to create or edit a skill now; use skill-smith after choosing a proposal.
You need a full retrospective of changes and technical debt; use insight-retro.
insight-skill-gap.example: /insight-skill-gap Check whether the caching work exposed a skill worth adding.
steps: Gather recent work and summarize patterns and technologies.
Read the current skill index.
Classify patterns as covered, incomplete, or absent and apply reuse criteria.
Present a targeted update or new-skill proposal for approval.
Only after approval, use skill-smith to create the chosen skills or apply targeted updates.

delegation.detail: Specifies a scan and proposal flow and no subagent step.

insight-skill-gap.outputs: Coverage findings and justified proposals, followed by skill creation or targeted updates only when approved.

insight-test-assumption.summary: Designs a bounded test that could support or disprove a decision-critical assumption; it does not run the test.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; possible slices include evidence retrieval, test design, and challenging the measurement or rule.

insight-test-assumption.outputs: A proposed test card and decision rule; no experiment execution, recruitment, spending, or deployment.

Describe information, signals, reliability, action changes, and costs.
Calculate EVSI/EVPI only when probabilities, payoffs, and signal accuracy are supported.
Recommend gathering information, deciding now, or remaining unresolved, with a stopping rule.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; useful slices include decision model, source reliability, and arithmetic checks.

insight-value-of-information.outputs: A supported information-value estimate or qualitative switching conditions with cost, gaps, and stopping rule.
